thread:
Maya (PM): ok dropping the new mock for the spend panel — focused on reducing visual noise when switching org vs project. link: https://figma.com/file/xyz (preview)
Jamal (Design): looking now. first impression: the left rail feels heavy compared to the chart. is the rail required at small breakpoints?
Maya (PM): the rail contains scope, time range, and quick invoice CTA. goal was one-click scope swap. open to collapsing it to a single chip on narrow widths.
Liam (Frontend): collapsing to a chip is fine, but need to think about keyboard focus and preserving the current scope state. we don't want the chip to hide info.
Jamal (Design): idea — collapsed chip shows scope + count (Org · 3 projects). expands into a popover with radio list. keeps hierarchy but reduces width.
Sophia (A11y): popover is ok, but ensure role="dialog" + aria-modal=false and focus trap only while interacting. also need visible focus styles for the chip.
Maya (PM): good catch. Jamal — can you show the microcopy inside the popover? worried about people confusing org vs workspace naming.
Jamal (Design): mock text: "Scope: which workspace's spend do you want to view?" then two rows: "Org (all projects) — 1.2M tokens" and "Project: payments — 120k tokens". thoughts?
Liam (Frontend): prefer shorter labels. maybe: "Organization — total tokens across projects" and "payments (project)". will implement tooltip for the longer explanation.
Sophia (A11y): tooltips need accessible triggers. if you use title attr it's not enough. add an info button with aria-describedby pointing to the tooltip content.
Maya (PM): about the chart area — we moved token breakdown stack from the right rail into a collapsible tray under the timeline. rationale: keeps timeline as primary and token split contextual. any concerns?
Jamal (Design): collapsing tray works visually. question: default collapsed or expanded? data suggests token split is next-most used after timeline on desktop.
Liam (Frontend): default expanded on desktop, collapsed on mobile. technically easy — use CSS grid with a row for the tray. here's a small CSS sketch:
```
.grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 320px 1fr; grid-auto-rows: auto; }
@media (max-width: 720px) { .grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .token-tray { order: 2; } }
```
Maya (PM): ok. invoices CTA — current mock places "Download invoice" inline inside the spend header. some PMs want it moved to the invoice drawer to avoid accidental downloads.
Jamal (Design): inline keeps discoverability for billing folks. maybe add a secondary placement: inline for admins, and inside drawer for everyone.
Sophia (A11y): two places is fine, but keep consistent labeling: "Download invoice (CSV)" vs "Download invoice" causes confusion. match them.
Liam (Frontend): auth-wise we already gate download by role. showing/hiding based on admin property is easy.
Maya (PM): token denom toggle — we have token vs cost. current toggle uses segmented control. accessibility note?
Sophia (A11y): segmented controls need role="tablist" semantics or use native radio groups. make sure keyboard arrows move selection, and state announced.
Jamal (Design): visually the selected state needs stronger contrast. current mock uses 10% darkening — bump to 20% and increase border radius for touch.
Liam (Frontend): noted. will use a11y focus outline and increased hit area for mobile.
Console Bot: deploy-preview available at https://deploy.preview/redwood/spend/1841122334 — visual tests: 12 failures (mostly spacing), 0 accessibility regressions flagged
Maya (PM): thanks bot. @Jamal can you patch spacing issues? and @Liam let's sync on the chip/popover keyboard behavior tomorrow 10am PT.
Jamal (Design): will update mock. I'll add explicit copy alternatives: "Organization (all projects)" and "Project: payments" and show tooltip copy.
Sophia (A11y): also add aria-live region for scope changes when switching so screen readers get context about data reload.
Liam (Frontend): will implement aria-live="polite" on the header summary. also will add a small test in cypress for focus order.
Maya (PM): lovely. aim to ship this as an experiment behind a feature flag next week. any blocking items?
Jamal (Design): none from design after I push updates.
Sophia (A11y): I'll review the new mock once Jamal pushes. no blockers.
Liam (Frontend): no blockers, but may need an extra hour for the tray animation.
Maya (PM): perfect — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short spec doc and the feature flag name.
